program_name: The full official English name used on unibz's own documents is 'International Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity' — this is the exact header of both the 2026/27 admission-information PDF and the 2026/27 brochure, and the hero heading of the programme page ('International Master in' on one line, 'Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity' on the next). The short form used in navigation, in the signed ranking list ('Admission to the Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity') and in the PDF filenames is 'Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity'. The programme is commonly abbreviated FSIA by the partner universities (the University of Parma files it under the URL slug 'cdlm-fsia'). The Italian ministerial/AlmaLaurea registration carries a bilingual title: 'Scienze degli alimenti per l'innovazione e l'autenticità - food sciences for innovation and authenticity (LM-70)'. unibz does NOT translate the name: the Italian and Ladin navigation both read 'Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity'. Delivered by the unibz Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences. LANGUAGE-VERSION NOTE, unusual for unibz: there is NO German version of the programme page at all (https://www.unibz.it/de/... returns HTTP 404), and the Italian and Ladin URLs return only a stub carrying the notice 'Siamo spiacenti, questa pagina non è disponibile in italiano. Vai alla pagina in inglese.' The English page itself displays 'This page is only available in English'. unibz's ranking-list index files the programme under the heading 'Late Application for Inter-university Masters', alongside Environmental Management of Mountain Areas, Energy Engineering and Industrial Mechanical Engineering.
level: Master (Italian 'laurea magistrale', second-cycle degree, EQF/NQF level 7). 120 ECTS over 2 years / 4 semesters, degree class LM-70. Entry qualification is a bachelor degree; at enrolment the Diploma Supplement must show 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. JOINT DEGREE, NOT A SINGLE-UNIVERSITY AWARD — this is the single most important structural fact about the programme and it is stated far more explicitly by the partner universities than by unibz. The University of Udine's official course page states verbatim: 'Il corso di laurea magistrale inter-ateneo, internazionale in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity è istituito tra la Libera Università di Bolzano (sede amministrativa), e le Università degli Studi di Udine e Parma con rilascio del titolo congiunto.' ('The inter-university, international master's degree course ... is established between the Free University of Bolzano (administrative seat) and the Universities of Udine and Parma, with the award of a JOINT DEGREE.') The 2021/22 University of Parma brochure says the same from the Parma side: the course 'is offered by tree [sic] joint Italian institutions (Free University of Bozen/Bolzano - administrative head, University of Parma and University of Udine) in cooperation with the University College Cork, Cork, Ireland and the Technical University of Munich, Munich, Germany.' PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATION — REAL AND VERIFIED: LM-70 is the Italian degree class that gives access to the state examination for the profession of Food Technologist. unibz's own Italian-language faculty page confirms it hosts that examination: 'Dal 2020 la Libera Università di Bolzano è sede degli esami di Stato per l'abilitazione all'esercizio della professione di Tecnologo alimentare.' ('Since 2020 the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano has been a seat of the state examinations for qualification to practise the profession of Food Technologist.') The 2021 Parma brochure states the requirement plainly: 'A professional practice exam called "esame di stato" in Italy must be passed to enroll in the Food Technologists professional register.' Graduates also gain access to doctoral study; unibz runs a directly related PhD in Food Engineering and Biotechnology in the same faculty. [uncertain] Whether a non-Italian graduate can sit the Tecnologo Alimentare state examination without additional steps, and how the joint diploma is physically issued (one parchment signed by three rectors versus three separate parchments), is not documented on any of the three universities' public pages and should be confirmed with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it).
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT, START TO FINISH, WITH NO SECOND OR THIRD LANGUAGE ANYWHERE IN THE PROGRAMME. This is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes. Brochure 'At a Glance', verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in English'. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' The only admission language requirement is English B2; there is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry, NO third-language B1 threshold gating exams, and NO exit/graduation language requirement. VERIFIED AT COURSE LEVEL, NOT JUST IN THE MARKETING TEXT: the unibz 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' page for 2026/27 lists every single teaching unit with an explicit language tag, and every one of them — the whole first year, all four second-year profiles, the three 'Mobility activity' units and all twelve free-choice courses — is tagged 'EN'. Not one course in the published catalogue is offered in German or Italian. This is a stronger guarantee than most unibz English-taught masters can show, and it holds even for the courses taught by University of Udine and University of Parma staff (e.g. Sabrina Moret, Sonia Calligaris and Lara Manzocco from Udine; Daniele Del Rio, Pedro Mena and Alessia Levante from Parma), which appear in the unibz catalogue in English. THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT IS TRILINGUAL BUT THE DEGREE IS NOT: Bolzano is officially bilingual German/Italian, and one of the programme's own published alumni testimonials notes taking optional German classes ('After a first year in Bolzano, where I took the opportunity to attend German language classes thanks to the University's trilinguism proactive setup'). Language Centre courses in German and Italian are available on a voluntary basis and are worth taking for the South Tyrolean food-industry job market, but they carry no admission or graduation consequence. [uncertain] For students who choose the Udine, Parma or University College Cork second-year profile, the admission documents do not state whether any locally-offered elective at the host institution might be delivered in Italian; the unibz catalogue tags all listed units EN, but the host universities' own wider elective menus are not reproduced there. Confirm with the degree course director before choosing a partner profile.
campus: PRIMARY CAMPUS: Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. The brochure 'At a Glance' box states simply 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano' — unlike the sister inter-university master EMMA, this programme does NOT advertise a second campus in its headline data, even though its second year can be taken abroad. TWO PHYSICAL SITES IN BOLZANO. (1) The main campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano (Advisory Service, tel. +39 0471 012100), with the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences Secretariat at Universitätsplatz 5 / piazza Università 5 (tel. +39 0471 017000, agriculture@unibz.it). (2) NOI TECHPARK, the South Tyrolean science-and-technology park on the southern edge of Bolzano, which houses this programme's teaching laboratories. Brochure, verbatim: 'The teaching laboratories of this master offer hands-on training in food production, analysis, and quality assessment. Located at NOI Techpark, they feature facilities for food processing, sensory evaluation, and chemical, physical, and microbiological analysis.' Students on this master therefore commute between the city-centre campus and NOI Techpark; unibz's own emergency-contact page treats 'Bolzano centro e NOI Techpark Bolzano' as two distinct locations with separate laboratory emergency numbers. This is a laboratory-heavy programme — the published 'Hands-on Experience' items include cheese-making, green-tea antioxidant extraction, iron/plant nutrition work, DNA extraction and natural-leavening bread work. SECOND YEAR: THE CAMPUS DEPENDS ON THE PROFILE CHOSEN. Year 1 (61 CP) is taken at unibz by everyone. From year 2 the profile determines the host institution: 'Innovation and Authenticity of Wines' stays at unibz in Bolzano; 'Food Quality Control and Management' is offered at the University of Udine (Friuli Venezia Giulia, ca. 300 km east of Bolzano); 'Nutrition Sciences' at the University of Parma (Emilia-Romagna, ca. 250 km south); 'Food Chemistry' at University College Cork, Ireland (School of Food & Nutritional Sciences). The programme page adds: 'Students will have the opportunity to spend up to two semesters in one of these European partner institutions.' The thesis (33 CP) may be carried out at unibz, at a partner university, at a foreign university or jointly, and is frequently co-supervised with a food company. NOT a Brixen-Bressanone or Bruneck-Brunico programme, and — unlike EMMA — NOT a fixed two-country programme: the Bolzano-only route through the Wines profile is fully available. [uncertain] It is genuinely unclear how much physical relocation the Udine and Parma profiles involve. The published 2026/27 unibz course catalogue lists the Udine profile courses (Advanced sample preparation techniques and analysis of food contaminants; Management systems of food safety and quality; Food structure and physical properties) and the Parma profile courses (Human Nutrition; Applied human nutrition; Industrial microbiology for food quality improvement) INSIDE the unibz course offering, taught by Udine and Parma professors, which may mean they are delivered in Bolzano by visiting staff rather than requiring the student to move. The University of Parma's page, by contrast, describes the profile-specific teaching as taking place at the partner universities in the third semester. This directly affects housing, cost of living and (for non-EU students) residence-permit planning, and must be confirmed with the Faculty before choosing a profile.
degree_class: LM-70 — 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari' (Food Sciences and Technologies), the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class for the food industry. CONFIRMED BY FOUR INDEPENDENT SOURCES, so the 'to be verified' flag in the research brief can be closed: (1) the unibz brochure 'At a Glance' box, verbatim 'Degree class: LM-70'; (2) the unibz programme page's own At a Glance block, 'Degree class: LM-70'; (3) the University of Udine course record, 'LM-70 Scienze e tecnologie alimentari'; (4) the AlmaLaurea/ministerial registration, 'Scienze degli alimenti per l'innovazione e l'autenticità - food sciences for innovation and authenticity (LM-70)', class 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari (LM-70)', also rendered by AlmaLaurea in English as 'LM 70 - Food Industry'. The signed 2026/27 ranking list confirms it functionally by using LM-70 in its double-enrolment illustration: 'the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-70/LM-70'. TWO TEMPLATE ERRORS IN UNIBZ'S OWN DOCUMENTS — worth knowing so they are not mistaken for real information. (a) The 2026/27 admission-information PDF's double-enrolment paragraph reads 'they do not belong to the same class (e.g. LM-73 and LM-73)' — LM-73 is the class of the sister programme EMMA, and the sentence is plainly copy-pasted from the EMMA template. (b) The signed ranking list repeats the double-enrolment rule twice, and its SECOND occurrence, in the 'Confirmation of study place and enrolment' section, reads 'e.g., LM-18/LM-18' — LM-18 is the Computer Science class used in the Software Engineering template. Neither error changes the programme's actual class, which is LM-70 in every substantive source. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (1) double-enrolment rule — a student may enrol in at most two programmes simultaneously, which must not share a class and 'must differ in at least two-thirds of their content'; (2) LM-70 is the class that opens the Italian state examination for Tecnologo Alimentare (Food Technologist), for which unibz has been an examination seat since 2020; (3) LM-70 is the natural second cycle above the Italian bachelor class L-26 (Food Sciences), which is why L-26 heads the list of directly-qualifying bachelor classes.

is_new_programme: NOT a new programme, but a relatively young one — roughly eight or nine intakes old. FOUNDED: the AlmaLaurea statistical record for this course gives the programme's inception as academic year 2018, i.e. the first cohort entered in 2018/19. That is consistent with the first graduate cohort appearing in 2020 (a two-year master started in 2018/19 graduates from 2020). GRADUATE COHORTS ON RECORD (AlmaLaurea): 2020 — 9 graduates; 2022 — 42 graduates; 2024 — 24 graduates; 2025 — 22 graduates. EVIDENCE OF MATURITY: (a) unibz publishes AlmaLaurea graduate-satisfaction and employability statistics for the programme — 90.9% completely or mostly satisfied, 90.9% would enrol on the same course again, 81.8% attended more than 75% of classes; employment 100% at one year after graduation with an average net monthly salary of EUR 1,447, and 92.9% at three years with EUR 2,049, job satisfaction 7.9/10 and 7.8/10 respectively; (b) a named Student Representative sits on the Course Council (Elena Greco); (c) the programme page carries six named alumni testimonials with current employers (VOG Products, Ferrero, F.lli Clementi, dsm-firmenich, Lavazza Group, Dolomites Milk). STRUCTURAL EVOLUTION — the programme has been materially reshaped since launch, and a candidate reading older material will be misled. In 2021/22, per the University of Parma brochure, it ran FIVE second-year profiles: 'Applied Engineering and Genetics' at unibz, 'Food Quality Control and Management' at Udine, 'Nutrition Sciences' at Parma, 'Food Chemistry' at UCC, and 'Food Packaging' at the Technical University of Munich. Today there are FOUR: the TUM packaging profile has been dropped (TUM survives only as an Erasmus exchange partner), and the unibz profile has been completely rebuilt and renamed from 'Applied Engineering and Genetics' (Food Processing Equipment / Genetics Applied to Foods / Sensors and Biosensors) to 'Innovation and Authenticity of Wines'. Individual first-year courses changed too — 'Unit Operations in Food Processing' and 'Food Chemistry' have gone, replaced by 'Insects as Novel Food', 'Innovative Food Technologies', 'Evaluation of Food Quality and Authenticity' and 'Computer applications in food sciences'. Places have grown from 35 EU + 5 non-EU (2021/22) to 40 EU + 8 non-EU, and tuition has FALLEN from EUR 1,350 (2024/25, per AlmaLaurea) to EUR 1,200. [uncertain] The 2018 inception year comes from AlmaLaurea's statistical record rather than from a unibz founding announcement; no unibz press release or founding decree was locatable, and the exact first-intake year could be 2018/19 or, less likely, 2017/18.
majors_tracks_study_plans:
ONE COMMON FIRST YEAR, THEN A CHOICE OF FOUR SECOND-YEAR PROFILES — chosen AFTER enrolment, not at application. There are no separate application codes, no separate quotas in the ranking list and no profile-specific entry requirements: the ranking list admits students to the programme as a whole. Programme page, verbatim: 'The first year mainly includes modules on Food Technology and Food Microbiology, which are common to all learning tracks. From the second year onwards, modules become specific to the profile chosen and you will be able to choose from four profiles and a range of free choice courses to customize your study program.'

YEAR 1 AT UNIBZ — 61 CP, entirely compulsory, identical for everyone: Innovation and Authenticity in Food Processing 12 CP (= Insects as Novel Food 6 + Innovative Food Technologies 6); Fermentations as Tools for Making Traditional and Innovative Foods and Beverages 8 CP; Environmental Chemistry towards Food Processing 8 CP; Food Value Chain Management 6 CP; Computer Applications in Food Sciences 3 CP; Reaction Kinetics in Food Processing 6 CP; Evaluation of Food Quality and Authenticity 6 CP; Starter and Functional Microbes for Innovation, Authenticity and Healthy Status 12 CP (= The natural microbial starters for innovation and authenticity 3 + Computational analysis in food microbiomes 3 + The food–human axis for driving the gut microbiome 6).

THE FOUR SECOND-YEAR PROFILES — 59 CP each, so that 61 + 59 = 120:
1. 'Innovation and Authenticity of Wines' (at unibz, Bolzano) — Processes and Technologies in Wine Production 6 CP (= Wine processing equipment 4 + Fermentation processes for the production of mountain wines 2); Wine Production and Sensory Analysis for Mountain Wines 6 CP (= Wine production processes and plants 3 + Sensory analysis approaches for mountain wines 3); Innovation and Authenticity for Winery Products 6 CP; Free Choice 8 CP; Thesis 33 CP.
2. 'Food Quality Control and Management' (at the University of Udine) — Advanced Sample Preparation Techniques and Analysis of Food Contaminants 6 CP; Management Systems of Food Safety and Quality 6 CP; Food Structure and Physical Properties 6 CP; Free Choice 8 CP; Thesis 33 CP.
3. 'Nutrition Sciences' (at the University of Parma) — Human Nutrition 6 CP; Applied Human Nutrition 6 CP; Industrial Microbiology for Food Quality Improvement 6 CP; Free Choice 8 CP; Thesis 33 CP.
4. 'Food Chemistry' (at University College Cork, Ireland, School of Food & Nutritional Sciences) — Mobility activity 1, 2 and 3 at 5 CP each; Free Choice 11 CP; Thesis 33 CP. This profile is capacity-limited: 'this master offers one dedicated path with the University College Cork, Ireland (5 available places with possible grants from local food companies)'.

FREE CHOICE COURSES — 'Students can choose courses of their choice. Every year the Faculty publishes the list of free choice courses offered.' The published 2026/27 menu is twelve courses, all in English: Food Allergens: Molecular Approaches and Regulatory Aspects (6 CP); Risk Assessment of Chemical Compounds (6 CP); Research and Development for Food Production (4 CP); Advanced Spectroscopic Techniques (4 CP); Advanced Machines and Plant in Agrifood Industry (3 CP); Cocoa and Coffee Fermentations (3 CP); Molecular Techniques in Food Technologies: from Biotechnology to Authenticity (3 CP); Quality of Horticultural Products (3 CP); Bakery and Confectionery Product Development: Nutrition Innovation and Sustainability (2 CP); Interplay Diet–Gut Microbiome–Human Health (2 CP); Bioinorganic Chemistry (2 CP); Novel and Functional Foods (2 CP).

OTHER VARIANTS: a PART-TIME enrolment route exists — 'Part-time enrolment allows you to reduce your study load... Students choose this option after enrollment (in October) and not during the application' — which extends the master to four years at roughly half the annual credit load. Separately from the profiles, two Erasmus exchanges are offered with the Technical University of Munich and Wageningen University & Research. No dual-study/apprenticeship model exists and no compulsory internship is imposed, though internships with the partner industry network are available.

[uncertain] Three open questions on this field. (1) NAMING INCONSISTENCY within unibz's own brochure: the course-description section calls the Udine profile 'Food Quality and Management' while the study-plan section on the next page calls it 'Food Quality Control and Management'; the latter matches the historical Parma documentation and is almost certainly correct. (2) HOW PROFILES ARE ALLOCATED is not published — whether the choice is free, first-come-first-served, or competitive is unstated, and it plainly must be competitive at least for the 5-place UCC path. (3) THE '5 available places' figure for UCC is given in the exchange paragraph, not in the study-plan section, and no allocation criteria are published.
english_only_accessibility:
OPEN — this is one of the most linguistically accessible programmes at unibz for an English-only candidate, and there is no hidden language trap anywhere in the two years. WHY IT IS FULLY OPEN: (a) the sole language requirement is English B2 ('Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2'); (b) there is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry, NO third-language B1 threshold gating exam attendance, and NO exit/graduation language requirement — this is an English-taught, not a trilingual, programme; (c) every teaching unit in the published 2026/27 catalogue, including all four second-year profiles and all twelve free-choice courses, is tagged 'EN'; (d) the application itself requires no motivation letter, no video, no portfolio and no interview, so there is no English-writing or English-speaking performance to prepare; (e) the thesis is written and defended in English.

WHERE THE REAL BARRIER LIES — AND IT IS NOT LANGUAGE COMPETENCE BUT LANGUAGE PAPERWORK. In the 2026/27 Early Bird round, EIGHT EU/parity applicants (IDs 152607, 155926, 153571, 155924, 152016, 148589, 154853, 147169) were excluded under the heading 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure.' Against 25 admitted, that is roughly a QUARTER of the EU pool lost on language documentation alone — and lost in a round that was UNDER-SUBSCRIBED (25 admitted against 35 places), meaning essentially all of them would have been admitted had their B2 evidence been in order. This is by far the most common way to fail this application, and it is entirely avoidable.

THE SECOND, MUCH HARDER BARRIER IS NATIONALITY, NOT LANGUAGE. See places_quotas and selection_scoring: the EU/parity list did not fill, while the non-EU-living-abroad list had 38 eligible applicants for 8 places — a 4.75x oversubscription with a cut-off of 87.08/95. For a Turkish applicant applying from Turkey this is the decisive fact about the programme: the language door is wide open and the quota door is very narrow.

DAILY LIFE: Bolzano is officially bilingual German/Italian, but unibz is a genuinely international campus and the food-science research groups work in English. A student choosing the Udine or Parma profile moves into a monolingual Italian-speaking environment for the second year; a student choosing UCC moves to an English-speaking one; a student staying on the Wines profile remains in Bolzano throughout. FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT specifically: a Gıda Mühendisliği, Ziraat Mühendisliği, Kimya/Kimya Mühendisliği, Biyoloji, Moleküler Biyoloji ve Genetik, Beslenme ve Diyetetik or Veteriner background will normally clear the academic threshold easily (only 30 ECTS in a very wide list of sectors is required), and an English-medium bachelor is recognised outright as C1 — which both satisfies the B2 gate and earns the +3 ranking bonus at zero cost.
admission_type:
RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / 'programmazione locale' in the University of Udine's registration), decided by a purely DOCUMENT-BASED, ARITHMETIC ranking. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video presentation and NO INTERVIEW. Together with EMMA this is one of the two simplest admission procedures at unibz.

MECHANICS, verbatim from the admission-information PDF and the signed ranking list (identical wording): 'If the number of eligible applicants exceeds the maximum number of available places (see section "Available places"), you will be assessed for admission based on your academic qualifications. The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points based on the: final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (for applicants already graduated); weighted grade average expressed out of 30 (for applicants not graduated yet). The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude). Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points. Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points.'

SO THE PROCEDURE HAS EXACTLY FOUR STAGES: (1) an ELIGIBILITY CHECK on the entry qualification — one of four Italian bachelor classes, or 30 ECTS across a very wide list of scientific sectors; (2) a LANGUAGE GATE at English B2, failure of which means exclusion from the procedure regardless of grade (8 EU applicants were excluded on this ground in Early Bird 2026/27); (3) an ARITHMETIC SCORE out of 95 derived from the bachelor grade, plus 2 for cum laude and plus 3 for a C1 English certificate; (4) a stated MINIMUM of 55/95.

A MANDATORY STRUCTURED EXCEL FILE must be uploaded: 'Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal.' Applications go through the unibz Application Portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup.

TIE-BREAK, in order: 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet. In the event of further equal score, the younger applicant will be given priority (art. 3 L. 127/1997).' This mattered in 2026/27: EU ranks 13 and 14 both scored 83.77, and non-EU waiting-list ranks 16 and 17 both scored 78.76.

ADMISSION COMMITTEE for 2026/27, from the signed ranking list: President Prof. Matteo Mario Scampicchio (who is also the Degree Course Director); Members Prof. Youry Pii and Dr. Ksenia Morozova. Appeals may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of publication.

HISTORICAL NOTE: the 2021/22 Parma brochure described access as 'Open access (Up to 35 EU students + 5 non-EU students)', i.e. capped but not competitive in practice. AlmaLaurea's records for 2024/25 and 2025/26 describe the committee as awarding 'up to 100 points'; the current unibz documents say 95. The scale appears to have been changed, and AlmaLaurea's figure should be treated as stale.
academic_requirements:
TWO ALTERNATIVE ROUTES, AND THE SECOND IS EXTRAORDINARILY PERMISSIVE BY UNIBZ STANDARDS. Admission-information PDF, verbatim preamble: 'In order to gain admission to this programme you need to possess an adequate knowledge of the basic disciplines of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology and fundamental knowledge of the subjects preparatory to the fundamental disciplines of this degree class. What is more, you need to hold one of the following qualifications:'

ROUTE 1 — a bachelor degree in one of four Italian degree classes: 'L-25 ex D.M. 270/2004 (Agriculture and Forestry) or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; L-26 (Food Sciences) or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; L-38 (Animal Production Sciences and Technologies) or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; L-GASTR (Sciences, cultures and policies of Gastronomy)'. Note the inclusion of L-GASTR, the new gastronomy class created in 2021 — unibz's own Bachelor in Food and Enogastronomy Sciences feeds directly into this master.

ROUTE 2 — the route almost every foreign applicant is assessed against: 'Or the previous career must have covered at least 30 ECTS credits in one or more of the following scientific sectors'. Only THIRTY credits, and they may come from a SINGLE sector. Compare EMMA (20 + 30 = 50 ECTS across two separately-defined blocks with a two-subject-area diversity condition) or the Master in Energy Engineering (85 ECTS across three blocks). This is the loosest curricular threshold of any unibz science master examined.

selection_scoring:
A SINGLE ARITHMETIC FORMULA WITH NO SUBJECTIVE COMPONENT. Verbatim (admission-information PDF and signed ranking list, identical): 'The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points based on the: final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (for applicants already graduated); weighted grade average expressed out of 30 (for applicants not graduated yet). The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude). Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points. Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points. If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet. In the event of further equal score, the younger applicant will be given priority (art. 3 L. 127/1997).'

THE SCORE THEREFORE HAS ONLY THREE INPUTS: the bachelor grade (or weighted average, if still studying), +2 for cum laude, +3 for a C1-or-better English certificate. Nothing else counts — not the CV, not work experience, not publications, not internships, not the reputation of the previous university, not a motivation letter. A candidate can compute their own score before applying.

DERIVED CONVERSION FORMULA — an INFERENCE from the published scores, not a published rule, but it fits every data point. This programme PUBLISHES INDIVIDUAL SCORES to two decimal places, which makes reverse-engineering possible. The best-fitting model is base = 5 × (grade out of 30) − 55, i.e. each whole grade point is worth 5 score points, capped at 95, plus the +2 and +3 bonuses. Evidence: (a) the published minimum of 55/95 maps exactly to a bachelor grade of 22/30, the same 22/30 floor unibz states explicitly in its engineering masters; (b) the maximum of 95 maps exactly to 30/30; (c) the same formula fits the sister programme EMMA's integer score distribution perfectly (65, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95 base values, each +3 when a C1 certificate is held). The competing hypothesis base = (grade/30) × 90 must be rejected, because it would imply waiting-list scores of 51.45 and 53.73 correspond to grades of 17.15/30 and 17.91/30 — below the Italian minimum passing grade of 18. RULE OF THUMB: roughly 22/30 to be eligible at all; a C1 certificate is worth about 0.6 of a grade point.

EFFECTIVE CUT-OFFS FOR 2026/27 EARLY BIRD — AND THE CENTRAL FINDING OF THIS RECORD:
— EU/parity: NO effective cut-off beyond the stated minimum. 25 applicants admitted against 35 places, so the list did NOT fill and every eligible EU applicant got in. The lowest admitted score was 60.04, roughly a grade of 23/30.
— Non-EU living abroad: the cut-off was 87.08/95, roughly a grade of 28.4/30 (or 27.8/30 with a C1 certificate). 38 eligible applicants competed for 8 places — a 4.75x oversubscription, with 30 people on the waiting list.
The gap between the two is enormous: a non-EU applicant needed to score 27 points HIGHER than the last admitted EU applicant. In practice a non-EU applicant from outside Italy needs something close to a first-class transcript to enter this programme, while an EU applicant needs only to be eligible.

STRATEGIC READING: (1) Because the score is 100% grade-driven, a modest GPA cannot be compensated with experience, research or a strong letter — there is nowhere to put them. (2) The C1 bonus is cheap and decisive at the margin: at a non-EU cut-off of 87.08, three points is well over a full rank position, and the waiting list is dense enough that +3 moves an applicant past several competitors. (3) An English-medium bachelor is recognised as C1 outright, so most Turkish applicants from English-medium programmes should receive the +3 at no cost simply by uploading a medium-of-instruction letter. (4) The tie-break rewards having already graduated, which argues for applying in the cycle after graduation rather than in the final undergraduate year. (5) A non-EU applicant who is close but not certain should consider whether they qualify for 'parity of treatment' (see parity_of_treatment) — moving from the non-EU list to the EU list is worth roughly 27 points of competitive advantage in this programme.

[uncertain] TWO UNRESOLVED ANOMALIES. (a) The 5g − 55 conversion is DERIVED, not published; treat it as a strong working model, not an official rule. (b) The published minimum of '55/95 points' was apparently NOT applied to the waiting list: non-EU waiting-list ranks 37 and 38 carry scores of 53.73 and 51.45, both below 55. Either the minimum is applied only at the point of actual admission, or the waiting list is published in full regardless. bonus_points:
ONLY TWO SCORE ADJUSTMENTS EXIST, and only one of them is realistically obtainable by a foreign applicant.

(1) C1 ENGLISH BONUS — verbatim: 'Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points.' Worth 3 points on a 95-point scale. CRUCIALLY, this can be earned WITHOUT SITTING ANY EXAM, because unibz recognises medium of instruction as equivalent to C1: 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1)' and 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1)'. A Turkish applicant from a 100%-English-medium programme who uploads a registrar's medium-of-instruction letter should therefore receive the 3 points at zero cost and zero risk. Applicants from 30%-English Turkish programmes cannot rely on this and should sit a certificate to C1 level — under unibz's recognised-certificate list that means IELTS 7.0–8.0, TOEFL iBT 95–113, Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE), C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) grade B or C, TOEIC Listening 490+/Reading 180+, PTE Academic 76–84, Aptis ESOL Advanced C1, or the unibz Language Centre internal C1 exam.

(2) CUM LAUDE ADJUSTMENT — 'The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude).' This is written for Italian-style 'con lode' graduations.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST HERE, contrary to other unibz programmes: NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is Software Engineering and Computing for Data Science, 3/2/1 points for a top-1000 / 1001-2000 / 2001-3000 university) — a bachelor from a highly ranked university earns nothing here; NO GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance); NO startup-project presentation bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points); NO video-presentation points (Energy Engineering, 10 points); NO CV or professional-experience points (Energy Engineering, 50 points). Work experience, publications, internships, Erasmus periods and reference letters are formally worth ZERO in this ranking. It is a grade-only competition with a single 3-point language sweetener.

[uncertain] Whether and how a Turkish 'yüksek onur derecesi' / 'onur derecesi', a British first-class degree, a US summa cum laude or any other national distinction is mapped onto the Italian 'cum laude' +2 is NOT stated anywhere in the documents. Because the published scores are given to two decimal places rather than in clean steps, it is also not possible to detect from the 2026/27 ranking list whether any +2 was actually awarded. An applicant with a national distinction should ask the Faculty Secretariat explicitly whether it counts, and should upload documentary evidence of it either way.
portfolio_and_materials:
NO PORTFOLIO, NO MOTIVATION LETTER, NO VIDEO, NO RESEARCH PROPOSAL, NO REFERENCE LETTERS — and not even a CV. This is among the leanest applications at unibz. The admission-information PDF lists exactly three uploads under 'In the application portal, you must upload', plus the ID required at account creation.

(1) QUALIFICATION EVIDENCE, verbatim: 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the final grade and passed exams (if graduated) or, if not graduated yet, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' Mandatory contents: 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles). For qualifications obtained abroad, also: scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable).'

THE GRADING-SCALE STATEMENT IS THE MOST COMMONLY OMITTED AND MOST DAMAGING OMISSION FOR A FOREIGN APPLICANT. Because the ENTIRE ranking score is computed from the grade converted to a /30 scale, unibz cannot score an application at all without knowing the source scale and both its endpoints. A Turkish applicant must supply an official statement showing the maximum achievable grade (4.00) and the minimum required to graduate (2.00) — ideally the registrar's printed grading-system legend on the transcript itself, not a self-written note. Getting this wrong risks either exclusion or an unfavourable conversion.

(2) THE EXCEL FILE — 'Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal.' This is the structured study-career template in which the applicant maps their own exams onto the qualifying scientific sectors, and it is the instrument the Committee uses to verify the 30-ECTS threshold. Treat it as mandatory and decisive; sister unibz programmes state explicitly that applications without a completed Excel file are not considered.

(3) ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATION at B2 or above, or medium-of-instruction documentation, or registration for a unibz Language Centre exam. Administrative form: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.'

(4) ID: 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.'

(5) FOR FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS ALSO THE DIPLOMA: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.'

(6) FOR PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS: a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno, or the renewal request if it has expired.

OPTIONAL BUT ADVISABLE, though not listed: course syllabi and content descriptions, because 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.'

FORMAT LIMITS: unibz publishes NO file-size cap, page limit or word limit for this programme — there is nothing to write and nothing to design, only documents to obtain. Contrast the 20 MB PDF portfolio cap in the Design programmes or the video limits in Energy Engineering.

HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' And, stated twice: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'
interview:
NO INTERVIEW. The 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the 2026/27 brochure and the signed 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list contain no reference to an interview, colloquium, videoconference, oral assessment or convocation of any kind — the word does not appear in any of the three documents. The Admission Committee (President Prof. Matteo Mario Scampicchio; Members Prof. Youry Pii and Dr. Ksenia Morozova) decides on uploaded documents alone, using the 95-point arithmetic formula.

There is likewise no 'adequacy of personal preparation' interview clause of the kind the Master in Energy Engineering operates, and no exclusion ground for non-attendance — contrast Energy Engineering, whose non-EU Early Bird list excluded applicants who 'did not participate in the mandatory interview'.

CONSEQUENCE FOR APPLICANTS: nothing needs to be prepared, rehearsed or scheduled after submission, and there is no time-zone or connectivity risk for overseas candidates. The flip side is that there is NO opportunity to explain or rescue a weak transcript, to argue that a non-obvious bachelor meets the 30-ECTS threshold, or to make a personal impression — the grade and the Excel file are the entire application. For a non-EU applicant facing a 4.75x oversubscription and an 87.08/95 cut-off, this is unforgiving: there is no route to compensate for a mid-range GPA.

HISTORICAL: no interview appears in the 2021/22 Parma documentation either, which described access simply as 'Open access (Up to 35 EU students + 5 non-EU students)' with online application. This programme appears never to have interviewed.
conditional_admission:
YES — conditional (provisional) admission for not-yet-graduated applicants is explicitly available, and the credit rules are unusually generous while the tie-break is unforgiving.

THE RULE, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'Applicants who do not yet have the required three-year degree may apply, but they must have the qualification by the enrolment deadline at the latest. Otherwise, they will be excluded from the procedure. Proof of possession of the qualification must be provided by the enrolment deadline.' The signed ranking list adds: 'Until your graduation, you will be admitted conditionally. You must have achieved your degree by the enrolment deadline, otherwise you will be excluded', and footnotes both admitted lists with: 'applicants who have not concluded their bachelor's degree are provisionally admitted: requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday).'

GENEROUS ASPECT — NO MINIMUM-CREDIT CONDITION. Unlike several unibz masters (≥120 ECTS already earned, or ≥140 for Data Analytics for Economics and Management), this programme imposes NO threshold of credits earned so far. Any enrolled bachelor student may apply, and their score is computed from the 'weighted grade average expressed out of 30' instead of the final grade.

STRICT ASPECT — THE TIE-BREAK PENALISES YOU: 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet.' In an oversubscribed round a not-yet-graduated applicant loses every tie. This was live in 2026/27: EU ranks 13 and 14 tied on 83.77, and non-EU waiting-list ranks 16 and 17 tied on 78.76, all decided by this rule or by the subsequent age rule.

DEADLINE FOR 2026/27: graduation must be completed by 13 October 2026, 12:00 midday.

SAFETY VALVE, verbatim: 'Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' The ranking list specifies the late enrolment request goes 'to the Rector'.

TWO FURTHER, SEPARATE RESERVATIONS APPLY. (a) Foreign degrees: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified' and 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded... If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' (b) All non-EU citizens living abroad: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' In other words, EVERY non-EU admitted applicant on the 2026/27 list holds a conditional place until the consulate communicates.

FINAL WARNING: 'If you have been admitted in the ranking list, but you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

[uncertain] The 2026/27 ranking list applies the provisional-admission footnote to both lists collectively rather than flagging individual applicants, so the proportion of not-yet-graduated admits in this cohort cannot be determined from the document.
ofa_rules:
NOT APPLICABLE. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an Italian instrument reserved for FIRST-CYCLE, open-access programmes where an applicant fails a compulsory entrance test; at unibz it is used in the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management, all tied to a mathematics test. This is a restricted-access SECOND-CYCLE programme with no entrance test, so the instrument cannot apply. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, nor the brochure, nor the signed 2026/27 ranking list mentions OFA, additional learning requirements, remedial obligations or credit debts, and the ranking list carries no OFA markers.

Italian law does not permit master-level admission with curricular credit debts to be settled after enrolment: the 30-ECTS threshold in the listed scientific sectors must be satisfied BEFORE admission. The only functional equivalent of a remedial route therefore sits on the pre-admission side — enrolling as an external/single-subject student to close a credit gap and re-applying in a later cycle. Note, however, that unlike the sister programme EMMA this programme's admission text does NOT signpost that route, so a candidate would have to find it themselves at unibz's single-subject-courses page.

A SEPARATE POST-ENROLMENT MECHANISM does exist and should not be confused with OFA: 'Recognition of credit points from previous studies — Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.' That is credit recognition in the student's favour, not a debt.
language_requirements:
ONE REQUIREMENT ONLY: ENGLISH AT B2 (CEFR) FOR ADMISSION. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.'

There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO graduation/exit language requirement. This is an English-taught, not a trilingual, programme, and the 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page' line at the end of the language section is boilerplate that applies to unibz generally, not to this degree.

THE LANGUAGE GATE IS A HARD KNOCK-OUT AND IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST CAUSE OF FAILURE IN THIS APPLICATION. Failure to prove B2 means exclusion from the admission procedure regardless of grade. In the 2026/27 Early Bird EU round, EIGHT applicants (IDs 152607, 155926, 153571, 155924, 152016, 148589, 154853, 147169) were listed under 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure. They may re-apply in the second session.' Against 25 admitted that is roughly a quarter of the EU applicant pool — and it happened in a round that did not fill its 35 places, so those candidates lost places that were sitting empty. By comparison, the sister programme EMMA lost only 2 applicants on language in the same cycle. Whatever the cause — late uploads, missing medium-of-instruction letters, certificates older than five years, or 'home edition' online exams — this is the failure mode to plan against.

B2 IS THE FLOOR, C1 IS THE SMART TARGET: a C1-or-better certificate adds 3 points to the ranking score. For a non-EU applicant facing an 87.08/95 cut-off, three points is a meaningful number of rank positions.

WHERE TO PROVE IT: in the Application Portal, sections 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', which become available only AFTER creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.

ADMINISTRATIVE FORM: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.'

DEADLINE MECHANICS: certificates that cannot be uploaded 'can be sent by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'. The Language Centre can be reached at language.centre@unibz.it, +39 0471 012400.
entry_levels_by_position:
ENGLISH B2 / no second language / no third language — in unibz's positional notation, B2 / none / none.

unibz expresses language requirements by POSITION (1st, 2nd, 3rd teaching language) rather than by named language. This programme has only ONE teaching language, English, in first position, required at B2. No level is required in a second or third language at any stage, because the programme is not trilingual.

COMPARISON ACROSS UNIBZ, to place this correctly: trilingual bachelors run B2/B2/none (Bachelor in Computer Science) or B2/B1/none (Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering); trilingual masters in Economics run C1/B2/none (Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, Master in Accounting and Finance). Against those, a single B2-in-English entry level is the least demanding language profile available at unibz, tied with the other fully English-taught masters such as EMMA, Energy Engineering and Software Engineering.

UNLIKE EMMA, THERE IS NO SECOND-LANGUAGE SHADOW REQUIREMENT. EMMA students spend year 2 at the German-speaking University of Innsbruck, where part of the elective menu is offered in German, so German has real practical weight even though it carries no formal level. Here, the second-year host options are Bolzano (bilingual, but all listed courses tagged EN), Udine and Parma (Italian cities, but the profile courses appear in the unibz English catalogue) and University College Cork (English-speaking). No second language reaches even informal necessity for the Bolzano or Cork routes.
exit_levels:
NO EXIT / GRADUATION LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, nor the brochure, nor the signed ranking list states any exit level; the entire 'Language requirements' section is headed 'Entry level (to gain admission)' and covers admission only.

This places the programme on the English-taught side of unibz's two-model system. The unibz Study Guide's C1/C1/B1 graduation model — certifying two languages at C1 and a third at B1 in order to graduate — applies to TRILINGUAL programmes. An entirely English-taught master does not include language requirements in other languages, and Language Centre courses are offered as an optional extra.

PRACTICAL SIGNIFICANCE: this removes the single biggest hidden risk of studying at unibz for an international student. In the trilingual programmes, students routinely gain admission and then cannot graduate on time because they have not certified the second and third languages. Here, once admitted with B2 English, no further language certification stands between the student and the degree — including for those who take the second year at Udine, Parma or University College Cork, and including the thesis, which is written and defended in English.

Students may still voluntarily take German or Italian at the unibz Language Centre, and one of the programme's own published alumni testimonials records doing exactly that ('I took the opportunity to attend German language classes thanks to the University's trilinguism proactive setup'). This is worth doing for the South Tyrolean and northern Italian food-industry job market — the industry partners include Dr. Schär, Loacker, Forst, Mila, VOG Products, Zuegg, Barilla and the Parmigiano Reggiano, Grana Padano, San Daniele, Montasio, Gorgonzola and Speck Alto Adige consortia — but it carries no graduation consequence.
third_language_exam_threshold:
NOT APPLICABLE — there is no second or third teaching language, therefore no third-language B1 threshold.

The rule this field is designed to capture — a B1 level in the third language required from the second semester of the first year in order to be allowed to sit exams — belongs exclusively to unibz's TRILINGUAL programmes. It does not appear in this programme's 2026/27 admission-information PDF, brochure or signed ranking list, and it cannot apply to a programme whose 'official teaching language is English' full stop. There is likewise no first- or second-language exam threshold gating exam attendance at any point in the two years.

The only language condition attached to this degree is the B2 English entry gate, which is settled before admission and never revisited. No language threshold arises in year 2 either, for any of the four profiles: the Bolzano, Udine, Parma and University College Cork routes are all covered by English-tagged units in the published unibz course catalogue, and none of the three partner institutions imposes its own language condition on students admitted through unibz, since unibz is the administrative seat of the joint degree.
proof_pathways:
FOUR ACCEPTED ROUTES TO PROVING ENGLISH B2, quoted verbatim from the admission-information PDF, in the order unibz lists them:

1. MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT HIGH SCHOOL — 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1). Foreign qualifications: If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' Note that this route is recognised at C1, not merely B2, so it also earns the +3 ranking bonus.

2. MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT UNIVERSITY — 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1). unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1). Foreign qualifications: If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' THIS IS THE BEST ROUTE FOR MOST INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS TO THIS PROGRAMME: it costs nothing, requires no exam booking, and is recognised as C1, thereby also delivering the +3 bonus. For a Turkish applicant from a 100%-English-medium bachelor, a registrar's letter on institutional letterhead stating that the degree was delivered entirely in English is sufficient and should be requested well before the application window opens.

3. A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE — 'a recognised language certificate (see the list of recognised certificates). If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' See certificate_rules for the governing rules and the accepted score bands.

4. THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAM — 'language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre. You can register for these exams online through the application portal (in the section "enrol for language exams") after you have filled out your application in the section "create/manage applications". The registration periods are indicated in the "Deadlines" section. If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.'

The unibz internal exam is recognised at B1, B2 and C1, and unlike international certificates the internal exam and the other 'further proofs' have UNLIMITED validity.

ADMINISTRATIVE FORM APPLYING TO ALL ROUTES: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.'

SEQUENCING TRAP: the language sections of the portal only unlock AFTER an application has been created. certificate_rules:
GOVERNED BY RESOLUTION OF THE UNIVERSITY COUNCIL No. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants' / 'Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università n. 16/2026'), published as a trilingual PDF at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf and verified on 2026-08-29.

GENERAL DISPOSITIONS, verbatim from the English text: 'In order to be recognised, an international certificate or any proof of language proficiency must meet the following requirements: 1. include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself; 2. indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade (and/or the detailed assessment is indicated on the certificate itself or by appropriate documentation faithful to the original by the certification organisation).'

THE FIVE RULES THAT MOST OFTEN DISQUALIFY A CERTIFICATE:
1. FIVE-YEAR VALIDITY — 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' Certificates listed under 'Further proofs' (unibz internal exams, the South Tyrolean bilingualism certificate, school-leaving and university qualifications) have UNLIMITED validity.
2. LOWEST SUB-SKILL DECIDES — 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' A candidate with three C1 sub-scores and one B2 sub-score is a B2 candidate.
3. NO COMPENSATION — 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.'
4. NO 'HOME EDITION' — 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' The starred exceptions in the English section are TOEFL, TOEIC and IELTS, which ARE accepted as home edition; most others are not.
5. NO DAAD, NO PARTIAL AND NO PRIVATE ATTESTATIONS — 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' Also excluded: certificates covering single skills from different organisations, course-attendance certificates, end-of-course tests from private providers, placement-test results, and attestations issued by individual teachers or lecturers.

ACCEPTED ENGLISH SCORE BANDS (from the English table of Resolution 16/2026):
— B2: IELTS (General and Academic) 5.5–6.5; TOEFL iBT 72–94; TOEIC Listening 400+ / Writing 150+; Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, B2 First for Schools, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade B or C, C1 Advanced (CAE) at level B2, C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) at level B2, B1 Preliminary (PET) grade A; MET B2 (all 4 skills); PTE Academic 59–75, PTE General Level 3; Aptis ESOL General B2 / Advanced B2.
— C1 (the level that earns the +3 bonus): IELTS 7.0–8.0; TOEFL iBT 95–113; TOEIC Listening 490+ / Writing 180+; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE), C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) grade B or C, B2 First (FCE) grade A, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade A, C2 Proficiency (CPE) at level C1; MET C1 (all 4 skills); PTE Academic 76–84, PTE General Level 4; Aptis ESOL Advanced C1.
— C2: IELTS 8.5+; TOEFL iBT 114–120; Cambridge C2 Proficiency (CPE) grades A/B/C, C1 Advanced (CAE) grade A, C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) grade A; ECPE; PTE Academic 85–90; Aptis ESOL Advanced C2.

A CLAUSE SPECIFICALLY RELEVANT TO THIS JOINT-DEGREE PROGRAMME: the 'Further proofs' section recognises, for unibz partner universities within Double or Joint Degree programmes, 'Attestati con indicazione del livello del QCER di esami superati presso i Centri linguistici delle università partner' — certificates stating a CEFR level from exams passed at the language centres of partner universities. Since this degree is formally a joint degree with the Universities of Udine and Parma, a language-centre certificate from either of those universities is directly usable.

UNIVERSITY QUALIFICATIONS AS PROOF: a bachelor (180 CFU) or master (120 CFU) taught with the language as one of the languages of instruction (at least 50% of credits) counts as B2; taught with the language as the main language of instruction (at least 75% of credits) counts as C1. This is the precise rule that lets an English-medium Turkish bachelor be recognised as C1.
application_deadline_eu:

It carried 5 EU places, plus any Early Bird places left unfilled: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' Because the 2026/27 Early Bird EU list admitted only 25 against 35 places, roughly 15 EU places were available in the Late round — an unusually favourable position for a late EU applicant.

3. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (ONLY FOR EU CITIZENS) — 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places. More information on additional sessions will be published in due course.' No additional session for this programme had been published as of 2026-08-29.

A SECOND CHANCE AFTER FAILURE IS EXPLICITLY GRANTED: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' The ranking list repeats this for the language-excluded applicants: 'They may re-apply in the second session.'

STATUS ON 2026-08-29: all published EU windows for 2026/27 have closed. The Late window expired on 2026-08-20 and its ranking list was still pending, due 'by 03/09/2026'. A prospective applicant reading this is targeting 2027/28. HISTORICAL STABILITY OF THE CALENDAR, useful for planning ahead: in 2021/22 the windows were 1 March – 28 April (Early Bird) and 19 May – 24 August (Late); in 2025/26 the Late deadline was 21 August. The pattern is extremely consistent — Early Bird opens in the first days of March and closes in the last days of April; the Late window runs from late May to the third week of August. application_deadline_non_eu:
ONE SINGLE WINDOW, AND IT IS THE EARLY BIRD WINDOW: 02/03/2026 – 28/04/2026, by noon local time (ISO: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 CET/CEST). Application fee: € 50.'

THIS IS THE HARDEST DEADLINE IN THE WHOLE RECORD AND THE MOST COMMON WAY A TURKISH APPLICANT LOSES A YEAR. There is no Late Application and no Additional Session for non-EU citizens living abroad — both are labelled 'only for EU citizens'. Missing 28 April means waiting a full twelve months. — Application 02/03–28/04/2026, noon.
— Language exams, if needed: 16/03/2026 (register 02–09/03) or 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (register 24/03–08/04). Note that the second sitting ends only one week before the application deadline, leaving almost no margin.

CRITICAL SEQUENCING POINT: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal.' The visa process cannot begin until the place is paid for, which leaves roughly four months between 05/06 and 13/10 to obtain a study visa from an Italian consulate — tight but workable, provided the consulate appointment is sought immediately.

WHO COUNTS AS NON-EU LIVING ABROAD — AND THE TRAP: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The ranking list repeats it: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' Given that the non-EU list in 2026/27 required 87.08/95 while the EU list required only 60.04, being misclassified through a missing upload is catastrophic. See parity_of_treatment.

parity_of_treatment:
A THIRD CATEGORY EXISTS BETWEEN 'EU' AND 'NON-EU', AND FOR THIS PROGRAMME IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY OTHER SINGLE FACTOR IN THE APPLICATION. In 2026/27 the EU/parity list admitted its lowest candidate at 60.04/95 while the non-EU list cut off at 87.08/95 — a 27-point gap. Qualifying for parity of treatment is therefore worth roughly five and a half grade points, far more than any bonus available in the scoring rubric.

WHO QUALIFIES, verbatim from the admission-information PDF under the heading 'EU-Citizens and equivalent — Considered as equivalent are':
'1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State;
2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request. Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.'

THE FIVE QUALIFYING PERMIT GROUNDS ARE THEREFORE: work, family reasons, political asylum, humanitarian asylum, religious reasons. A STUDENT PERMIT DOES NOT COUNT, and neither does a tourist visa. This is the crucial limitation: a Turkish citizen already in Italy on a student permit for a bachelor degree does NOT gain parity of treatment for this master and must compete on the non-EU list.

WHO THIS MATTERS FOR AMONG TURKISH APPLICANTS: a Turkish citizen holding an Italian permesso di soggiorno per lavoro subordinato, lavoro autonomo, motivi familiari (including a permit obtained through marriage to an Italian or EU citizen), asilo politico or motivi religiosi applies on the EU timetable, with three possible windows instead of one, no EUR 50 application fee, no Universitaly step and no visa process — and, decisively in this programme, against a list that did not fill. A Turkish citizen holding dual citizenship with an EU member state, or with Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino or the Vatican, is treated as an EU citizen outright.

OPERATIONAL WARNING: parity of treatment is not automatic and is not inferred from an address. It exists only if the permit scan is uploaded in the Application Portal. An expired permit is acceptable only if the renewal request is attached. Given the 27-point competitive gap in this programme, an eligible applicant who forgets this upload effectively forfeits their place.
places_quotas:
48 PLACES IN TOTAL, SPLIT ACROSS THREE SEPARATE QUOTAS — and the split is the most consequential fact in this record for an international applicant.

OFFICIAL FIGURES from the admission-information PDF, section 'Available places':
— EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application 35; Late Application 5. Total EU: 40.
— Non-EU citizens (living abroad): Early Bird Application 8. There is no Late or Additional quota for non-EU applicants.
The brochure 'At a Glance' box collapses this into 'Places available: 40 EU + 8 non-EU', and AlmaLaurea records the total as 48.

Unfilled Early Bird EU places roll forward: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.'

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN 2026/27 EARLY BIRD — the two sides of this programme behave like two different degrees:
— EU/PARITY: 25 applicants admitted against 35 places. THE LIST DID NOT FILL. No EU waiting list was published. Eight further EU applicants were excluded for failing the language requirement, so the total eligible-and-scored EU pool was around 33 against 35 places. The lowest admitted score was 60.04/95. Roughly 15 EU places (10 unfilled Early Bird + 5 Late) therefore carried into the Late window.
— NON-EU LIVING ABROAD: 8 admitted against 8 places, with a WAITING LIST OF 30 FURTHER APPLICANTS (ranks 9 to 38). That is 38 eligible applicants for 8 places, an oversubscription ratio of 4.75x, and the cut-off score was 87.08/95 — implying a bachelor grade of roughly 28/30 on the derived conversion. The last waiting-list score was 51.45.

COMPARISON WITH THE SISTER PROGRAMME EMMA in the same cycle makes the point sharply: EMMA admitted 31 EU applicants against 35 places with a 1-person non-EU waiting list, whereas this programme has a 30-person non-EU waiting list. Among unibz's inter-university agricultural masters, this is by a wide margin the most competitive for non-EU candidates and among the least competitive for EU candidates.

WAITING-LIST MECHANICS, verbatim: 'Applicants from rank 9 are on the waiting list and will only be able to join the programme if the admitted people do not secure their admission by the deadline. Those on the waiting list will be contacted by e-mail as of 8 June 2026 in case a spot opens up.' The trigger is failure by an admitted applicant to pay the first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon: 'If you do not meet this deadline, you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted.'

STRATEGIC READING FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT APPLYING FROM TURKEY: eight places, thirty-eight competitors, and a cut-off around 28/30. Plan on needing a genuinely strong transcript, secure the +3 C1 bonus, apply in the cycle after graduating (the tie-break favours graduates), and treat the waiting list as a realistic outcome worth staying available for through early June. If any route to parity of treatment exists, it is worth more than everything else combined.

[uncertain] Two unknowns. (1) It is not published how far the non-EU waiting list actually moved in 2026/27 — the number of admitted applicants who failed to pay by 05/06/2026 is not disclosed, so the true effective cut-off may have been lower than 87.08. required_documents:
AT APPLICATION — four items, exactly as enumerated in the admission-information PDF:

0. VALID ID, at account creation: 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.'
1. QUALIFICATION: 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the final grade and passed exams (if graduated) or, if not graduated yet, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' Mandatory contents: 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles). For qualifications obtained abroad, also: scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable).'
2. EXCEL FILE: 'Please use the file available in the application portal.' The structured study-career template mapping exams onto the qualifying scientific sectors — the instrument by which the 30-ECTS threshold is verified.
3. ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATIONS 'at least of level B2', or medium-of-instruction evidence, or registration for a unibz Language Centre exam.
PLUS, for foreign qualifications: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.'
PLUS, for parity-of-treatment applicants: a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno, or the renewal request if expired.

AT ENROLMENT, for holders of a foreign university degree — three base items plus a country-dependent recognition package:
— 'degree diploma of your Bachelor';
— 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)';
— 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'.
Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein — ARDI Statement of Correspondence; (b) non-EU Lisbon Convention signatories — ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU non-signatories — CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND CIMEA Statement of Verification. See credential_recognition.
For non-EU citizens living abroad, additionally: the entry visa for study/university and, after arrival, the residence permit handed in to the Student Office.

DOCUMENTS AN APPLICANT MIGHT EXPECT BUT DOES NOT NEED: no CV, no motivation letter, no reference letters, no research or thesis proposal, no portfolio, no video, no GRE/GMAT report, no proof of funds at application stage (that belongs to the visa process), no health certificate.

STRONGLY ADVISABLE THOUGH NOT LISTED: course syllabi and content descriptions, because 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary'; and, for any applicant claiming a national academic distinction, documentary evidence of it, since the cum laude mapping is undefined.

CHECKLIST FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT, in the order the items take longest to obtain: (1) the registrar's medium-of-instruction letter — free, fast, and worth +3 points; (2) the official English transcript WITH the printed grading-scale legend showing 4.00 maximum and 2.00 minimum — this is the item most often missing and it is load-bearing for the entire score; (3) the diploma and Diploma Supplement showing ≥180 ECTS and access to master studies; (4) CIMEA Statement of Comparability and Statement of Verification — Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so the ARDI route plus CIMEA verification applies, and CIMEA processing takes weeks, so start immediately after admission; (5) the completed portal Excel file.

HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents.' 'Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'
application_fee:
EUR 50, charged ONLY to non-EU citizens living outside Italy, and non-refundable. Admission-information PDF, verbatim, under 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy)': 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' The unibz page for non-EU degree-seeking applicants states the refund position explicitly: '50€. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.'

NO APPLICATION FEE IS CHARGED to EU citizens, to citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State, or to non-EU citizens holding a qualifying Italian residence permit (work, family, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons) — all of whom apply under parity of treatment. This is one more concrete advantage of the parity route, on top of the three application windows and the far lower score threshold.

The fee is separate from and additional to the EUR 600 first instalment of tuition that secures an admitted place, and from the EUR 16 revenue stamp included in that instalment. It is a pure administration charge and buys no priority.
tuition_or_fees_link:
EUR 1,200 PER YEAR, in two instalments. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'Fees amount to € 1200. 1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes. If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' The brochure 'At a Glance' box states 'Tuition fees: ca. € 1200 per year'. Over the two-year degree the total is therefore approximately EUR 2,400.

THE FIRST INSTALMENT DOUBLES AS THE PLACE-SECURING PAYMENT. For 2026/27 Early Bird it had to be paid by 05/06/2026 at noon, and for the Late round by 11/09/2026 at noon. Missing it forfeits the place to the next person on the ranking list.

EXEMPTIONS, verbatim: 'Exemption from the tuition fees is granted to: Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year. Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government.' And: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.'

REFUND POSITION: 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling. If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund, except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country.' This last exception is the safety net for a Turkish applicant who pays, then fails to obtain a visa.

CONTEXT — THIS IS CHEAP AND HAS GOT CHEAPER. EUR 1,200 is a flat fee unrelated to income, nationality or ISEE, which is unusual in the Italian system and strongly favourable to international students, who at most Italian state universities pay income-assessed fees that can be far higher without an ISEE-parificato. It is also lower than it used to be: AlmaLaurea records an annual cost of EUR 1,350 for the 2024/25 cohort and EUR 1,200 for 2025/26, and the 2019/20-era figure for the sister programme EMMA was EUR 1,347.50.

OFFICIAL FEE PAGES: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ (unibz Study Guide, Tuition Fees).

[uncertain] PART-TIME FEES. unibz's part-time enrolment scheme, which this programme's page advertises, is described in secondary summaries of the Study Guide as halving the annual tuition while roughly halving the annual credit load and extending a master to four years, with the option chosen in October after enrolment rather than at application. The exact part-time fee for this programme in 2026/27 was not confirmed on a primary unibz page during this verification and should be checked in the Study Guide before relying on it.
