scholarships_grants:
NO SCHOLARSHIP IS ATTACHED TO ADMISSION ITSELF. There is no merit award in the ranking procedure, no fee waiver for high scorers and no international-student scholarship run by the Faculty. Funding comes from three separate places.

1. THE PROVINCIAL STUDY GRANT (the main instrument) — awarded not by unibz but by the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol's Office for the Right to Study (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario), on the basis of income and family circumstances, with amounts commonly cited in the range EUR 1,680–6,960 per year. Recipients also get their tuition back: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees' and 'If you are able to receive a grant from the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, you receive the reimbursement of monies paid for the academic year.' Applications go through the Province's e-government service; the South Tyrolean Students Association (sh.asus) assists with them.

THE NON-EU BARRIER, WHICH MATTERS ENORMOUSLY HERE: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.' A Turkish student arriving on a study visa is therefore NOT eligible in the first year and becomes eligible only from the second year — by which time, on the Udine, Parma or Cork profiles, they may no longer be resident in South Tyrol at all. For a non-EU student on this programme, first-year funding must be assumed to be entirely self-financed, which dovetails with the visa requirement to prove roughly EUR 24,000 of means for a master.

2. MERIT SCHOLARSHIPS — after the first year, students achieving an average of 27/30 become eligible for merit-based rather than income-based awards. Non-EU citizens holding a time-limited residence permit face a stricter residence condition for the merit route (at least two years of uninterrupted residence in the Province of Bolzano at the application deadline), which in practice puts merit scholarships out of reach for most non-EU students on a two-year master.

3. PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC AND INDUSTRY MONEY — this is where this master differs from most unibz programmes, because of its unusually deep industrial partnership. The brochure states of the Irish profile: 'this master offers one dedicated path with the University College Cork, Ireland (5 available places with possible grants from local food companies).' Separately, the thesis is routinely co-funded and co-supervised by industry: 'The programme is supported by industries belonging to AssoImprenditori Alto Adige - sezione Alimentari - and Südtiroler Bauernbund... This partnership will allow students to write their research thesis with joint tutorship from both the university and the food industry.' The named participating companies are Assolatte, Barilla, Consorzio Gorgonzola, Consorzio Grana Padano, Consorzio Parmigiano Reggiano, Consorzio Prosciutto di San Daniele, Consorzio Montasio, Consorzio Tutela Speck Alto Adige, Despar, Dr. Schär, Forst, Loacker, Mila, Pan, Unione Parmense degli Industriali, VOG Products and Zuegg. Alumni testimonials confirm this route in practice — one graduate conducted the master thesis at DSM Nutritional Products in Switzerland and another started at Lavazza Group through the thesis.

4. ERASMUS+ MOBILITY GRANTS are available for the exchanges with the Technical University of Munich and Wageningen University & Research, on the standard Erasmus terms.

5. FEE EXEMPTIONS rather than grants: full exemption for students with a recognised disability under Law 104/1992 or a disability of 66% or above, and for foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship.

[uncertain] The EUR 1,680–6,960 provincial range and the 27/30 merit threshold come from secondary summaries of unibz's Study Guide rather than from a primary provincial decree verified in this pass, and provincial amounts are re-set annually. The 'possible grants from local food companies' attached to the University College Cork path are not quantified anywhere, no eligibility criteria are published, and it is not stated whether they are awarded by unibz, by UCC or by the companies directly.
credential_recognition:
A THREE-TIER SYSTEM DETERMINED BY THE COUNTRY OF THE BACHELOR DEGREE, applied at ENROLMENT rather than at application. Verbatim from the admission-information PDF and repeated in the signed ranking list.

BASE REQUIREMENTS FOR EVERY FOREIGN DEGREE: 'degree diploma of your Bachelor'; 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)'; and 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'.

THEN, BY EDUCATION SYSTEM:
(a) 'EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein: Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy'.
(b) 'Non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy and Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA)'.
(c) 'Non-EU countries that are not signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA) and Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA)'.

FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT, CATEGORY (b) APPLIES. Türkiye is a signatory to the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so the route is the ARDI Statement of Correspondence PLUS a CIMEA Statement of Verification — the cheaper and faster of the two non-EU routes, since the ARDI database statement is generated automatically rather than assessed. Note that CIMEA verification requires the issuing university to respond to CIMEA's authenticity check, which is the step most likely to introduce delay; a Turkish applicant should initiate it immediately after paying the first instalment in June rather than waiting until the October enrolment deadline. No translation into Italian is needed if the diploma and supplement are issued in English, which most Turkish universities can provide on request.

TIMING AND CONDITIONALITY: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified.' 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents. Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

A SEPARATE, EARLIER RECOGNITION STEP HAPPENS AT APPLICATION STAGE and should not be confused with the above: the Admission Committee independently maps the applicant's exams onto the qualifying scientific sectors for the 30-ECTS threshold, 'based on the contents of the exams passed during your previous study career', using the portal Excel file and, if requested, course descriptions. That is an academic eligibility judgement by the Faculty, not a legal recognition of the diploma.

Also note unibz's general service page for this, https://www.unibz.it/en/services/recognition-foreign-qualifications, and the separate post-enrolment rule on transferring credits: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.'
non_eu_visa_process:
A FIVE-STAGE PROCESS THAT CANNOT BEGIN UNTIL THE PLACE IS PAID FOR, compressed into roughly four months.

STAGE 1 — APPLY IN THE ONLY WINDOW. Early Bird only, 02/03–28/04/2026 at noon, with the EUR 50 non-refundable application fee. There is no second chance in the same cycle.

STAGE 2 — SECURE THE PLACE. Ranking list by 27/05/2026; first instalment of EUR 600 by 05/06/2026 at noon.

STAGE 3 — UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT, MANDATORY AND SINGLE-CHOICE. Verbatim: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking list is blunter: 'Non-EU citizen living abroad will also have to apply on the Universitaly portal of the Italian Ministry of Universities and Research. In Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only. Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.' A candidate admitted to two Italian programmes must therefore choose one on Universitaly and abandon the other.

STAGE 4 — THE STUDY VISA, obtained from the Italian embassy or consulate in the applicant's country. NO GUARANTEES ARE GIVEN, and unibz says so twice: 'Please note that preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Likewise, obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme.' unibz's non-EU page adds that admission 'does not guarantee an appointment at the diplomatic-consular Italian representation'. PROOF OF FINANCIAL MEANS, from the unibz page for non-EU citizens living abroad: living costs of 'at least € 800 per month' in the Bozen-Bolzano area, with a total for a MASTER programme of 'at least € 24,000' (the bachelor figure is EUR 36,000, reflecting the three-year duration), on top of tuition of 'ca. 1200€ per year (to be paid in two instalments)'. The consulate also requires the official communication of admission, which the Italian consulate abroad sends directly to unibz — and until it does, admission remains provisional: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.'

STAGE 5 — ARRIVAL, RESIDENCE PERMIT AND ENROLMENT. 'According to Italian law, within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit: as soon as you arrive, get in touch with the Advisory Service and you will be given the necessary information for starting the procedure. Once you will obtain your residence permit (permesso di soggiorno), you have to hand it in at the Student Office personally or via e-mail.' Online enrolment must be completed between 10/07 and 13/10/2026 at noon, with late enrolment to 11/12/2026 only if places remain.

WORKING WHILE STUDYING: a student residence permit allows part-time work 'for no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year'. Note that this same student permit does NOT confer parity of treatment for admission purposes, and does not by itself unlock the provincial study grant.

THE ONE REFUND PROTECTION: 'If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund, except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country.' So the EUR 600 first instalment is recoverable in the specific case of a visa failure — but the EUR 50 application fee never is.

A CONSIDERATION UNIQUE TO THIS PROGRAMME'S STRUCTURE: a non-EU student who chooses the second-year 'Food Chemistry' profile at University College Cork moves from Italy to Ireland, and one who chooses Udine or Parma may move within Italy. An intra-Italy move requires updating the residence permit's registered address; a move to Ireland raises a separate Irish immigration question that none of the three universities' public pages address. This should be raised with the unibz Advisory Service and with the Faculty before committing to the Cork path.

[uncertain] Health-insurance requirements, the exact consular documentary checklist and any Irish immigration route for the UCC profile were not documented on the unibz pages verified here, and the EUR 24,000 master figure is unibz's own guidance rather than a consular rule — the consulate in Ankara or Istanbul may apply a different threshold.

DATA VINTAGE. Everything in this record describes the 2026/27 cycle, from unibz documents footed 'Latest update: 24.07.2026' and from the signed 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list, all retrieved on 2026-08-29. On that date the 2026/27 cycle was effectively closed: both EU windows and the single non-EU window had expired, and only enrolment formalities remained. A reader planning an application is planning for 2027/28, for which NO dates, quotas or fees have been published. The observed calendar has been stable across four cycles (Early Bird opening in the first days of March and closing in the last days of April; Late running from late May to the third week of August), so those ranges are a reasonable planning basis, but they are extrapolations.

THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT UNRESOLVED QUESTION — WHERE THE SECOND YEAR PHYSICALLY HAPPENS. unibz's brochure lists 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano' with no second campus, and the 2026/27 unibz course catalogue lists the Udine and Parma profile courses INSIDE the unibz offering, taught by Udine and Parma professors, all tagged EN. The University of Parma, by contrast, describes profile-specific teaching as taking place at the partner universities in the third semester, and unibz's own programme page says students 'will have the opportunity to spend up to two semesters in one of these European partner institutions'. These two pictures are not reconcilable from public sources. The difference matters for housing, cost of living, residence-permit address updates and — for the University College Cork path — a possible move to a different country's immigration system. This must be settled with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it, +39 0471 017000) before a candidate commits.

THE JOINT-DEGREE MECHANICS ARE UNDOCUMENTED. That the award is a joint degree ('rilascio del titolo congiunto') is stated plainly by Udine and by Parma and is not in doubt. But the underlying inter-university convention is not published by any of the three universities, and nothing public explains how the diploma is issued, whether the partner universities levy any fee, how the 5 University College Cork places are allocated, or whether profile choice is free or competitive.

TEMPLATE ERRORS IN UNIBZ'S OWN DOCUMENTS, recorded so they are not mistaken for data: the admission-information PDF's double-enrolment example says 'LM-73 and LM-73' (EMMA's class), and the ranking list's second statement of the same rule says 'LM-18/LM-18' (Software Engineering's class). The correct class is LM-70, confirmed by the brochure, the programme page, the University of Udine and AlmaLaurea, and used correctly in the ranking list's first statement of the rule.

NAMING INCONSISTENCY: the brochure calls the Udine profile 'Food Quality and Management' on page 3 and 'Food Quality Control and Management' on page 4. The latter matches the 2021 Parma documentation.

THE SCORING CONVERSION IS DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED. The model base = 5 × (grade out of 30) − 55, capped at 95, with +2 cum laude and +3 for C1, fits the published minimum (55 = 22/30), the maximum (95 = 30/30) and the sister programme EMMA's integer distribution, and it is the only model tested that does not produce impossible sub-18/30 grades for the lowest waiting-list scores. It should nonetheless be treated as a strong working model rather than an official rule.

AN UNEXPLAINED ANOMALY IN THE RANKING LIST: the stated minimum is 55/95, yet non-EU waiting-list ranks 37 and 38 carry scores of 53.73 and 51.45. Unlike EMMA's list, this one has no 'below the minimum score' exclusion section, so it cannot be determined whether the minimum is applied only at the moment of admission or whether the waiting list is simply published in full. Practical effect is limited — nobody near the bottom of a 30-person waiting list was ever going to be admitted — but the rule's exact operation is unclear.

CONFLICTING SECONDARY DATA. AlmaLaurea records the admission committee as awarding 'up to 100 points' for both 2024/25 and 2025/26, while unibz's own current documents say 95; AlmaLaurea also gives EUR 1,350 as the 2024/25 annual cost against EUR 1,200 now. Where AlmaLaurea and unibz disagree, the unibz document governs. AlmaLaurea's 'five distinct profiles' phrasing is likewise stale — there are four.

SOURCES THAT COULD NOT BE READ. The University of Parma's live course page (corsi.unipr.it) serves a JavaScript CAPTCHA human-verification wall to automated clients and was not accessed; the Parma information in this record therefore comes from the University of Udine's parallel page, from Parma's own 2021/22 PDF brochure on its albo pretorio, and from search-engine extracts of the Parma page. The unibz grade-statistics page for this programme returns HTTP 200 but loads its figures dynamically and yielded no static content, so no exam-grade or final-grade distribution could be captured — a gap relative to the EMMA record, which has one.

FIGURES TAKEN FROM SECONDARY SUMMARIES RATHER THAN PRIMARY PAGES: the provincial study-grant range of EUR 1,680–6,960, the 27/30 merit threshold, the two-year residence rule for non-EU merit applicants, and the part-time fee halving. All are consistent with unibz's Study Guide as summarised, but the primary Study Guide pages redirected in ways that prevented direct capture during this pass, and provincial amounts are re-set annually.

NOT DOCUMENTED ANYWHERE: how a non-Italian 'with honours' distinction maps onto the +2 cum laude bonus; whether a non-Italian graduate can sit the Tecnologo Alimentare state examination; health-insurance requirements for the study visa; the amount of the late-payment fine on the second instalment; and the founding year, which is taken from AlmaLaurea's 'inception 2018' record rather than from a unibz announcement.
